title: ABMF: Adaptive Bonsai Merkle Forests for Efficient Integrity Verification in Secure Persistent Memories
problem: Non-volatile memory security verification using Merkle trees requires expensive tree traversal for MAC and counter updates on every memory write, creating significant latency and performance overhead.
motivation: Secure persistent memories (encrypted NVM with integrity verification) require fast MAC/counter updates and verification. Traditional BMT (Bonsai Merkle Tree) designs suffer from deep tree traversal costs during memory writes.
method: Forest structure extending Bonsai Merkle Trees by identifying intermediate tree nodes as additional root nodes. Extra roots maintained in secure processor reduce effective tree height for updates and verification.
key_novelty: Multi-root Merkle forest structure significantly reducing tree traversal depth during memory updates while maintaining security properties.
contributions: Adaptive forest structure for Merkle trees (ABMF)
Reduced tree height for memory update operations
Improved performance and reduced search space over existing BMT methods
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative improvements provided (% latency reduction, specific speedups, or memory overhead metrics). No silicon results.
primary_theme: Optimized data structures for secure memory verification
